A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Quantization without Tears study. Their text, equations, tables, figures and Appendices A–B are readable and support a complete comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original QwT experiments on image classification, detection, segmentation, multimodal recognition, image generation and language tasks, including Tables 1–13 and generated-image examples.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental outcomes in Tables 1–13 and Figures 2–4. Retention from v1 does not change their status as original empirical results.

M1.justification: The blockwise linear compensation, closed-form initialization, R-squared gate, QAT adaptation and optional finetuning procedure are unchanged. Appendix A retains the same classification-plus-feature-distillation objective.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same ImageNet classification and generation tasks, COCO detection/segmentation, CLIP recognition, WikiText2/C4 language evaluations, eight commonsense QA tasks and MMLU. Appendix coverage is also unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership matches in every corresponding table, including RepQ-ViT, Percentile, PTQ4ViT, Q-ViT, MinMax, GPTQ, Q-DiT and appendix PTQ4DM. IGQ-ViT and CL-Calib remain the same paper-sourced comparison rows.

E3.justification: Section 4 and Appendix A retain identical calibration counts, quantization settings, finetuning budgets, metrics and testing procedures. Examples include 512 images for QwT classification initialization and 128 C4 sequences of 2048 tokens for LLM calibration.

E4.justification: The QAT initialization analysis, qualitative generation comparisons and examples in Figures 2–4, and diffusion-setting comparisons in Table 13 are retained unchanged. No ablation, robustness test or supplementary analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged. Both present point estimates without repeated-run counts, error bars, confidence intervals or significance tests; neither adds evaluation seed information.

E6.justification: All entries in Tables 1–13 and the qualitative images and findings match. For example, Table 7 retains FID 6.06 for Q-DiT + QwT at W4A8, and Table 8 retains QA average 65.18 for GPTQ + QwT.

T1.justification: The quantization definitions, compensation formulation and closed-form solution in Equations 1–6 are unchanged, as are the mathematical reasoning and assumptions. No theorem, proof or derivation is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about speed, accuracy, simplicity and generality through lightweight compensation modules. The added Contributions paragraph concerns author roles and does not revise the scientific contributions.

C2.justification: Both retain the cumulative-error compensation explanation, the explanation for closed-form initialization failing on QAT models, and the same applicability and overhead discussions. No substantive interpretation or limitation is added or changed.

D1.justification: v3 adds a public code-availability statement and implementation link at the end of the abstract, absent from v1. Existing implementation details and Appendix A are unchanged. The PDFs establish the new access information, but not the repository's contents or usability.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, research positioning and all 56 cited works are unchanged. Differences in reference page backlinks reflect text reflow rather than citation additions or removals.

P1.justification: v3 adds a short code-availability sentence and an unnumbered Contributions section assigning author responsibilities. The scientific prose, terminology and existing section sequence otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The additions cause limited page and column reflow, including shifts around the conclusion, references and appendix opening. Figure content, table structures and captions are retained; appendix pages 12–15 render identically.

improvement.justification: The added implementation location improves code-access documentation, and the author-role statement improves attribution transparency. These are limited gains: the methods, experimental evidence and scientific discussion remain unchanged, and actual code usability cannot be established from the supplied PDFs.
